frontMatter.introduction: This Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) Manual outlines the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework for THE AML RightSource Group of Companies (hereafter referred to as 'the Company' or AMLRS). As a leading provider of financial crime compliance solutions, AMLRS is committed to integrating ESG principles into its operations, governance, and corporate responsibility initiatives. This manual serves as a guide for employees and stakeholders, ensuring alignment with sustainability goals, ethical business practices, and regulatory compliance. It defines procedures for environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and corporate governance, reinforcing the company's dedication to long-term value creation. By implementing these SOPs, AMLRS aims to enhance transparency, mitigate risks, and foster a sustainable business environment in line with global ESG standards.
frontMatter.scope: This SOP Manual on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices applies to all employees and relevant functions across AML RightSource Group of Companies' global operations. It establishes a consistent framework for integrating sustainability, environmental responsibility, social practices, ethical business conduct, and governance principles into the Group's operations. The Manual supports responsible business practices, regulatory compliance, risk management, and alignment with applicable international ESG expectations, while allowing for local legal and regulatory requirements to be addressed where applicable.

blocks.text: AMLRS upholds the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and ethical behavior in the workplace. This Code of Conduct establishes clear expectations for employee behavior, ensuring a respectful, inclusive, and compliant work environment.

This procedure applies to all AMLRS employees, contractors, interns, and visitors across all office locations. It governs workplace behavior, ethical responsibilities, and compliance with corporate policies, ensuring consistency and fairness at every level.

responsibilities: Enforces the Code of Conduct, investigates complaints, and addresses violations effectively.
Ensure compliance, guide employees on expected behavior, and handle misconduct fairly.
Follow the Code of Conduct, report unethical behavior, and maintain a professional work environment.

body.text:
Employees must maintain professionalism and treat others with courtesy and respect at all times.
Harassment, discrimination, and bullying are strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated at AMLRS.
A cooperative work environment is promoted to ensure smooth collaboration between all employees.
Constructive feedback and open communication are encouraged to resolve conflicts professionally.

Employees must uphold honesty, integrity, and transparency in all professional interactions.
Conflicts of interest must be disclosed immediately to avoid ethical or legal concerns.
Fraud, bribery, and corruption are strictly prohibited and will result in severe disciplinary action.
AMLRS expects employees to act in the company's best interest at all times without personal bias.

AMLRS promotes diversity, equity, and inclusion by ensuring equal opportunities for all employees.
Discrimination based on gender, race, religion, disability, or any other factor is strictly prohibited.
Any incidents of bias, prejudice, or discrimination must be reported to HR for immediate action.

Harassment, including sexual harassment, verbal abuse, or intimidation, is strictly prohibited.
Employees must report any incidents of harassment to HR immediately for proper investigation.
Regular training and awareness sessions are conducted to ensure a safe and respectful workplace.

Employees must safeguard company and client information, ensuring data privacy at all times.
Compliance with data protection regulations is mandatory, and breaches will result in disciplinary action.
Sensitive company information must be shared only with authorized personnel to prevent data leaks.

Company resources, including equipment and technology, must be used responsibly for business purposes.
Personal use of company resources must not interfere with work productivity or efficiency.
Misuse, damage, or theft of company property is subject to strict disciplinary measures.

Employees must adhere to all applicable laws, industry regulations, and internal company policies.
Any legal violations, misconduct, or unethical actions will be addressed with disciplinary action.
AMLRS conducts regular training programs to reinforce employee awareness of laws and corporate policies.

Employees must represent AMLRS professionally on all public and social media platforms.
Confidential company information must not be shared online, ensuring data security and protection.
Posting offensive, defamatory, or misleading content about AMLRS is strictly prohibited.

narrative.text:
Employees must report any Code of Conduct violations to HR or their immediate supervisor without delay.
All reports are handled confidentially, and retaliation against reporting employees is strictly prohibited.
Disciplinary actions may include verbal warnings, written notices, suspension, or termination as required.
AMLRS ensures a fair and transparent investigation process to address violations promptly and effectively.

body.text: Hazardous Waste Collection: Hazardous waste such as batteries and expired toners should be collected separately in designated IT support and maintenance areas for proper handling.
E-waste Collection: Electronic waste, including old laptops, keyboards, and cables, should be stored in IT and storage rooms for vendor-managed collection.

Cleaning staff empties general waste and recyclable bins twice daily (morning and evening) and hazardous waste bins weekly to ensure proper categorization and prevent overflow.
Electronic waste is stored in designated IT storage rooms before vendor pickup, ensuring proper handling and compliance with disposal regulations. All general waste is collected daily and directly sent to waste trucks for disposal, minimizing onsite accumulation.
Waste generation data is monitored through regular audits, tracking waste volumes by type and adjusting bin placement or disposal frequency accordingly to optimize collection efficiency.

General waste is collected daily from all office locations and transported via designated waste collection trucks to appropriate municipal processing centers, ensuring timely and efficient disposal.
Electronic waste, including outdated computers and peripherals, is securely stored in IT storage rooms until it is handed over to authorized recycling vendors for environmentally safe disposal.
Hazardous waste, such as batteries, is stored in designated containment areas and collected bi-weekly by licensed disposal partners to ensure regulatory compliance.
Recyclable materials like paper, plastics, and metals are sorted at collection points and sent to certified recycling facilities to promote resource conservation.

steps.heading: Enhancing Resource Efficiency and Minimizing Waste

body.text:
AMLRS promotes a paperless office by transitioning to digital documentation and cloud-based file storage, significantly reducing paper consumption.
Office supplies such as binders, folders, and printer cartridges are collected, checked for usability, and redistributed within departments to minimize excess waste.
Furniture and packaging materials are repurposed when possible, extending their usability and preventing unnecessary disposal.
Unused materials from office renovations or furniture upgrades are donated to nonprofit organizations or repurposed internally to maximize resource use.
Employees are encouraged to return used stationery to designated collection points, where they can be inspected, refurbished, and reused.

steps.heading: Optimizing Material Usage to Reduce Waste

body.text:
Procurement policies focus on ordering only necessary supplies to avoid surplus stock and reduce material wastage.
AMLRS encourages employees to use electronic alternatives instead of printed documents, implementing digital signatures and online collaboration tools to minimize paper reliance.
AMLRS ensures office resources are used efficiently by implementing strict procurement guidelines to prevent over-purchasing and unnecessary waste generation. Office supplies such as paper, folders, and packaging materials are reused whenever possible, extending their lifespan before disposal. A centralized inventory system is maintained to monitor supply usage, preventing surplus accumulation and promoting responsible material consumption.
Double-sided printing is encouraged when printing is necessary, reducing paper consumption across office locations.
Department heads review supply usage quarterly to identify further opportunities for reducing material consumption.

steps.heading: Integrating Sustainable and Eco-Friendly Office Supplies

body.text:
AMLRS prioritizes sourcing office supplies from vendors who offer biodegradable, recycled, or sustainably produced materials, ensuring a lower environmental footprint.
Cleaning products used across all locations are non-toxic and eco-friendly, reducing harmful waste output.
Disposable plastics are being phased out in office cafeterias and break rooms, replaced with reusable cutlery, cups, and containers to promote sustainability.
Office stationery, such as pens and notebooks, is sourced from suppliers offering refillable or recycled-material options.
Employees are encouraged to bring their own reusable water bottles and coffee cups, reducing reliance on single-use plastics.
AMLRS does not purchase plastic water bottles for office use, instead providing filtered water stations and reusable glass bottles for employees.
Office furniture is purchased from eco-friendly certified partners, ensuring sustainability in procurement and reducing environmental impact.

steps.heading: Encouraging Internal Exchange and Resource Sharing

body.text:
AMLRS has developed a platform for employees to exchange and claim surplus office supplies, preventing unnecessary purchases and reducing overall waste.
Departments can request and share available office items rather than discarding surplus supplies, ensuring responsible resource allocation.
A designated storage area is maintained for surplus supplies, where employees can deposit and retrieve items as needed, maximizing material reuse.
Employees are encouraged to return used office supplies, such as binders and file folders, to the resource-sharing area for others to reuse.
Internal awareness campaigns highlight the benefits of the resource-sharing platform, ensuring greater participation.
At global locations, AMLRS also implements this practice using the "GreenDesk Exchange" platform, allowing cross-office sharing and reducing waste across regions.

steps.heading: Maximizing IT and Office Equipment Lifespan

body.text:
AMLRS refurbishes and redistributes IT equipment such as laptops, monitors, and peripherals within the organization before considering disposal.
Functional hardware is reassigned to other departments to extend usability, minimizing electronic waste generation.
Outdated but functional equipment is donated to charitable organizations or responsibly recycled through certified partners, ensuring sustainable disposal.
Preventive maintenance programs are in place to extend the life cycle of IT and office equipment, reducing premature disposal.
Secure data-wiping procedures are followed before repurposing IT hardware, ensuring data privacy while enabling reuse.

rows.definition: Human rights are the fundamental freedoms and entitlements that every individual possesses by virtue of being human. These rights are universal, inalienable, and indivisible, ensuring dignity, fairness, equality, and respect for all individuals. They are protected under international frameworks such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR).

sections.title: Internal and External Stakeholder Human Rights

blocks.text:
Internal Stakeholders: Internal stakeholders, including employees, management, and shareholders, have the right to fair wages, a safe working environment, non-discrimination, and freedom of association. Companies must ensure ethical labor practices, diversity, and equal opportunities within their operations.
External Stakeholders: External stakeholders, such as suppliers, customers, local communities, and regulatory bodies, must be treated with fairness and respect. Organizations should prevent human rights abuses in supply chains, ensure responsible sourcing, and support community rights, such as access to clean water and fair economic opportunities.

Right to Equality: Every person is entitled to equal treatment and protection under the law without discrimination.
Right to Freedom of Expression: Individuals have the right to express their opinions and ideas freely, within legal boundaries.
Right to Fair Working Conditions: Employees should work in a safe environment with fair wages and reasonable working hours.
Right to Education: Every individual has the right to access quality education without discrimination.
Right to Privacy: Individuals have the right to personal privacy, including protection from unlawful surveillance and data misuse.

sops.title: HUMAN RIGHT DUE DILIGENCE IN CUSTOMER SCREENING

blocks.text: To establish a formalized due diligence process to screen customers utilizing financial services, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and mitigating risks associated with financial crimes, sanctions violations, and human rights abuses.

This procedure applies to all customer onboarding and transaction monitoring activities within AMLRS and is mandatory for all relevant departments responsible for compliance, risk management, and customer verification.

responsibilities: Conducts customer screening, ensures adherence to due diligence protocols, and reports suspicious activities.
Assesses and mitigates financial and reputational risks associated with customer transactions.
Collects necessary documentation and provides initial verification before customer approval.
Reviews and approves high-risk customer cases and ensures strategic alignment with regulatory policies.

substeps.text: Obtain and verify identity documents (e.g., government-issued IDs, passports, business registrations).
Conduct Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures, including address verification and source of funds assessment.
Maintain updated customer records in accordance with regulatory requirements.
Screen customers against global sanctions lists, including OFAC, EU, UN, and other applicable regulatory lists.
Utilize automated tools for real-time sanctions monitoring and flagging of potential matches.
Escalate positive matches to the Compliance Team for further investigation and necessary action.
Categorize customers into risk levels (low, medium, high) based on their financial activities, geographic location, and business nature.
Conduct Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for high-risk customers, including in-depth background checks and transaction monitoring.
Apply additional verification measures for customers from high-risk jurisdictions or industries.
Regularly review customer transactions to detect suspicious patterns indicative of money laundering, fraud, or sanctions evasion.

AMLRS is committed to ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data by implementing robust data privacy and cybersecurity measures. This SOP outlines the protocols to safeguard sensitive information, prevent cyber threats, and ensure compliance with applicable data protection regulations.

This procedure applies to all AMLRS employees, contractors, and third-party service providers handling company data. It covers data storage, access control, cybersecurity protocols, incident response, and employee responsibilities regarding data protection.

responsibilities: Implements and monitors cybersecurity measures, conducts risk assessments, and responds to security incidents.
Ensures adherence to data protection laws and internal policies.
Follow security protocols, report security incidents, and maintain data confidentiality.
Adhere to AMLRS cybersecurity policies and contractual data protection requirements.

rows.definition: Data that can identify an individual, such as name, email, and financial details.
Confidential business information, trade secrets, and intellectual property.
A fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive information through deceptive emails or messages.
Malicious software, including viruses, ransomware, and spyware, designed to disrupt or gain unauthorized access.
Restricting data access based on job roles and responsibilities.

body.text:
AMLRS categorizes data as public, internal, confidential, or highly sensitive and applies appropriate security controls.
Sensitive data is encrypted during storage and transmission to prevent unauthorized access.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enforced for accessing critical systems and confidential data.
Role-based access control (RBAC) is implemented to ensure employees only access data relevant to their responsibilities.
Periodic access reviews are conducted to prevent unauthorized data exposure.

Firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and endpoint security solutions are deployed to protect the company’s network.
Regular security patches and software updates are applied to mitigate vulnerabilities.
Employees are required to use strong, unique passwords and update them periodically.

AMLRS has a structured incident response plan to detect, report, and mitigate security breaches.
All security incidents must be reported to the IT Security Team immediately.
A forensic analysis is conducted after any breach to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.

Employees undergo mandatory cybersecurity awareness training, including phishing simulations and best practices for handling sensitive data.
Regular reminders and training sessions reinforce adherence to security policies.

AMLRS evaluates vendor security practices before granting access to company systems.
Vendors handling sensitive data must comply with AMLRS security requirements and undergo regular security assessments.

AMLRS adheres to relevant data privacy laws, such as GDPR, CCPA, and other applicable regulations.
Data retention policies ensure personal and business data is stored only for the required period and securely disposed of afterward.

blocks.text: AMLRS continuously reviews and enhances its data privacy and cybersecurity measures to address emerging threats and regulatory updates. Regular audits, penetration testing, and employee feedback contribute to the continuous improvement of security protocols.

The IT Security Team and Compliance Department review this SOP annually to ensure effectiveness.
Security audits and employee feedback drive improvements in data protection strategies.
AMLRS implements new security technologies and updates policies as needed to maintain a strong cybersecurity posture.

blocks.text: To ensure regulatory compliance and mitigate financial risks, a structured due diligence process is essential. This procedure outlines key steps for identifying, assessing, and monitoring customers to prevent illicit activities and maintain transparency.

body.text:
Obtain identity documents such as government-issued IDs, passports, or business registrations.
Verify the authenticity of these documents to ensure legitimacy.
Perform Know Your Customer (KYC) checks, including:

substeps.text: Address verification (residential or business)
Employment and financial background assessment

body.text:
Assess the source of funds and the intended use of financial services to detect potential illicit activities.
Cross-check customer details with regulatory databases to confirm compliance with Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter-Terrorist Financing (CTF) regulations.

Screen customer information against global sanctions lists, including OFAC, EU, UN, and domestic regulatory bodies.
Use automated compliance tools to monitor real-time updates on sanctions lists.
Flag any potential matches and escalate them to the Compliance Team.
Conduct further investigations on flagged entities and determine necessary actions, such as account suspension or regulatory reporting.

substeps.text: Financial activities

sops.title: PROCEDURE FOR REVIEWING AND APPROVING SENSITIVE TRANSACTIONS

blocks.text:
Establish a standardized approval process for sensitive transactions involving external parties, ensuring transparency and compliance with ethical and regulatory standards.

Define permissible transaction types, approval thresholds, and reporting requirements to mitigate potential conflicts of interest.
This procedure applies to all AMLRS employees, particularly those in decision-making roles or those responsible for approving sensitive transactions.

responsibilities: Reviews and ensures all sensitive transactions align with company policies and applicable laws.
Conduct initial reviews and recommend approval for sensitive transactions within their respective teams.
Maintains transaction records, ensures proper documentation, and verifies approvals before processing transactions.

rows.definition: Transactions involving gifts, travel expenses, entertainment, or other exchanges that may influence decision-making or create an appearance of preferential treatment.
Any individual or entity outside AML RightSource, including clients, vendors, and regulatory authorities.

body.text:
Defining Sensitive Transactions:

Includes, but is not limited to:

Gifts, travel, or entertainment provided to or received from external stakeholders.
Sponsorships, charitable donations, or grants given to entities with business ties to AMLRS.
Transactions exceeding USD 60 for gifts or USD 120 for travel-related expenses require formal approval.
Employees must submit proposed sensitive transactions to their department head, including details such as purpose, value, and involved parties.

steps.heading: Approval Steps

body.text:
Departmental Review: The department head evaluates the request for policy compliance, ethical considerations, and conflict-of-interest risks.
Compliance Officer Review: Transactions exceeding the defined thresholds require additional review and written approval to ensure regulatory compliance.
Executive Review: High-value or high-visibility transactions (over USD 250) must be approved by the Executive Committee and documented accordingly.

steps.responsible: Department head; Compliance Officer; Executive Committee

substeps.text: Departmental Review: The department head evaluates the request for policy compliance, ethical considerations, and conflict-of-interest risks.

body.text:

Entertainment Restrictions: Entertainment expenses must align with AMLRS policy limits and be approved in accordance with ethical standards.

blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes the framework for assessing the performance of procurement personnel within AMLRS. The objective is to ensure that procurement activities align with the company's strategic sourcing objectives, supplier compliance standards, and sustainability commitments.

This SOP applies to all AMLRS employees involved in procurement activities, including the acquisition of goods and services. It also covers direct supervisors and the broader Supply Chain Management (SCM) team.

rows.definition: An individual responsible for procuring goods or services for AMLRS, ensuring adherence to procurement policies and sustainability commitments.
Procurement decisions that prioritize environmental and social responsibility.
Metrics used to measure a buyer's effectiveness in achieving procurement goals.
Ensuring vendors adhere to ethical, regulatory, and corporate standards.

responsibilities: Conduct procurement activities in line with AMLRS's policies, supplier management framework, and sustainability guidelines while meeting KPIs.
Oversee buyer performance, provide guidance, and evaluate performance scorecards.
Ensure procurement aligns with sustainability principles and update evaluation criteria as necessary.

substeps.text: Regularly review procurement strategies and corporate goals to ensure buyer KPIs remain relevant.
Incorporate corporate priorities such as sustainability, supplier compliance, and cost efficiency into evaluations.
Procurement Efficiency: Assess the buyer's ability to source goods/services efficiently while maintaining cost-effectiveness and quality.
Supplier Compliance: Verify vendor adherence to AMLRS's regulatory, ethical, and sustainability standards.
Cost Management: Measure cost savings through strategic sourcing and negotiations.
Sustainable Procurement: Prioritize suppliers that align with environmental responsibility and waste management practices.
Annual Assessments: Buyer performance will be reviewed every year by supervisors based on KPI achievements.
Scorecards: Buyers will receive performance scorecards covering procurement efficiency, supplier compliance, and sustainability efforts.
Supervisor Review: Supervisors will validate scorecards and provide constructive feedback.
Supervisors will offer detailed feedback, highlight improvement areas, and recommend necessary training.
If performance targets are unmet, an improvement plan will be developed collaboratively.

rows.record: Quarterly performance reports to the SCM team (sustainability achievements and areas requiring attention)

blocks.text: Supplier Engagement and Management

Maintain active supplier communication to ensure compliance with AMLRS's procurement and sustainability criteria.
Conduct periodic supplier audits to confirm adherence to ethical and environmental standards.
Sustainability in Procurement

Prioritize suppliers offering sustainable products/services, including eco-conscious solutions.
Encourage vendors to implement waste reduction initiatives.
KPI Customization

KPIs will be tailored based on the buyer's procurement role:
Procurement Efficiency: Cost savings, timely deliveries, and purchase order management.
Supplier Compliance: Percentage of vendors meeting regulatory and sustainability standards.
Cost Management: Cost reductions through optimized purchasing strategies.
Sustainability: Sourcing eco-friendly materials and promoting supplier adherence to environmental best practices.

Annual performance appraisals will summarize quarterly reviews and assess a buyer's contribution to AMLRS's procurement and sustainability goals.

sops.title: SUPPLIER ESG DUE DILIGENCE, ASSESSMENT & ENGAGEMENT

blocks.text: The objective of this document is to establish a consistent approach for assessing, monitoring, and improving supplier performance across relevant environmental, social, ethical, and governance aspects.
This document applies to all AMLRS suppliers, contractors, service providers, and other relevant third parties engaged by AMLRS.

responsibilities: Coordinates supplier onboarding, due diligence, assessments, documentation, performance monitoring, and follow-up actions.
Establishes relevant ESG requirements, supports supplier assessments and audits, reviews findings, and monitors improvement actions.
Conducts supplier assessments and on-site audits, verifies supporting evidence, documents findings, and follows up on corrective actions.
Provide accurate information and required documents, participate in assessments and worker feedback activities, and implement corrective actions within agreed timelines.
Provides oversight of significant supplier ESG risks, assessment findings, and corrective actions, and supports appropriate escalation where required.

blocks.text: AMLRS applies a combination of assessment, verification, engagement, and monitoring activities to evaluate supplier performance. Depending on the supplier's risk profile and business relationship, these activities include:

body.text: Suppliers complete structured assessments covering relevant environmental, labor, human rights, health and safety, ethical, and governance practices.
Where required, AMLRS conducts on-site assessments to verify supplier practices and identify areas requiring improvement.
AMLRS obtains feedback from supplier workers, where appropriate, to understand workplace conditions and identify concerns that may not be evident through management-level assessments.
Relevant policies, certifications, records, licenses, training information, and other supporting evidence are reviewed as part of supplier due diligence.
Identified gaps or non-conformities are communicated to suppliers and followed up through corrective action plans and supporting evidence.
AMLRS communicates its expectations and engages with suppliers to address identified risks and encourage responsible business practices.
Supplier performance and identified risks are periodically reviewed to determine whether additional assessment or follow-up is required.

rows.record: Supplier Worker Feedback Forms and results
Corrective Action Plans and closure evidence

blocks.text: AMLRS maintains relevant records of supplier due diligence and monitoring activities, including, where applicable:

AMLRS uses supplier assessment, audit, worker feedback, and corrective action results to improve supplier ESG performance.
Identified gaps are followed up with suppliers to support timely corrective action and responsible business practices.

The Compliance, Procurement, and ESG/Sustainability Teams periodically review the supplier due diligence process for effectiveness and compliance.
The process is updated, where necessary, based on regulatory changes, stakeholder feedback, assessment findings, and emerging ESG risks.
Relevant personnel receive appropriate training and guidance on supplier ESG requirements and responsible sourcing practices.
